extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, policymakers, Congress, and stakeholders in the intellectual property community (patent/trademark practitioners, IP offices)
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level performance and operational standards, metrics, and program requirements related to patent office activities (international cooperation, work-sharing/PPH, IT systems, security remediation, workforce/telework, training, and capacity-building). Used to evaluate progress toward USPTO strategic and management goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT system improvement proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to improve the WIPO-administered PCT system, including implementing an electronic document system, implementing a process for improving prior art searches with respect to the international application, and providing WIPO assistance in training of examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are USPTO-proposed enhancements to streamline international filing and examination under PCT to benefit applicants and examiners; used as advocacy/negotiation points with WIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) criteria and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH allows an applicant who receives a positive ruling on patent claims from one participating office to request accelerated prosecution of corresponding claims in another participating office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include faster patent grants in multiple jurisdictions, reduced expense, and leveraging other offices’ work to improve examination efficiency and quality. Includes bilateral PPHs and Global PPH framework (single centralized set of common requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative PPH filings (PPH usage metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracking cumulative PPH filings over time (monthly/yearly counts such as those in Figure 9 showing month/year of first PPH petition filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure uptake and utilization of PPH programs (including outreach effectiveness, e.g., PPH pilot with Brazil/INPI-BR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global PPH participation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Global PPH creates a centralized framework of common requirements to replace many bilateral PPH arrangements; offices must accept requests under the Global PPH pilot program to participate (the United States is one of 24 offices accepting Global PPH requests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation implies adherence to the common set of standards to simplify administration and filing for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives and principles for internationally harmonized patent system
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an 'objectives and principles' document specifying principles for an internationally harmonized patent system and goals such a system should aim to achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a policy framework for substantive patent law harmonization among like-minded IP offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial Design 5 (ID5) harmonization goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve consistency in industrial design registration policies, catalog office practices, promote interoperable procedural frameworks, and protect emerging designs such as GUIs, animations, and other new technology designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ID5 forum outcomes guide harmonization efforts among the five largest industrial design offices to improve global design registration consistency and interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: TM5 ID List project (harmonized identifications for goods/services)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a harmonized pick-list of identifications for goods and services acceptable across participating trademark offices; expand number of ID entries and translate into multiple languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides pre-approved IDs (>16,000 developed to date) for applicants to use in trademark applications; invites participation from non-TM5 offices to broaden harmonization.

rubrics_metrics.name: TM5 common status descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a common set of 'status descriptors'—terms and corresponding symbols—that indicate the status of trademark applications and registrations across partner offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deployment (e.g., on USPTO's TSDR tool) improves clarity and interoperability for applicants and stakeholders tracking application/registration status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad faith trademark filings definition and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Bad faith trademark filings refer to filings made for unfair purposes, exploiting the absence of another person’s trademark registration in a given country or region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TM5 bad faith filings project coordinates partner offices to combat such filings; identifies problematic filings and supports enforcement/countermeasures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity-building metric: Number of foreign government officials trained
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the number of foreign government officials trained on best practices to protect and enforce intellectual property (Table 14: targets and actuals by fiscal year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks training reach and effectiveness; FY targets provided (e.g., target 5,000 for FY2016) and actual enrollment used to evaluate program performance; FY2016 used blended e-Learning and in-person courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-specific action plan progress metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure: Percentage of prioritized countries for which country teams have made progress on at least 75% of action steps in the country-specific action plans (Table 15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess implementation of bilateral/multilateral assistance and outreach; target commonly set at 75% and actual progress reported annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimensions for country action-step progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress of action steps was measured along these dimensions: (1) institutional improvements of IP office administration for advancing IP rights, (2) institutional improvements of IP-enforcement entities, (3) improvements in IP laws and regulations, and (4) establishment of government-to-government cooperative mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four dimensions define what constitutes meaningful progress in country-specific action plans and are the basis for the 75% progress metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide policy advice and technical expertise to other U.S. agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO provides policy advice and technical expertise on domestic and international IP matters to OMB, USTR, OSTP, IPEC, other Commerce bureaus, and federal agencies (e.g., advising on Special 301 reports, WTO accession, trade negotiations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance measured by participation in negotiations, provision of drafted provisions, technical analyses, and interagency coordination outcomes (no single numeric metric given on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for negotiating and implementing IP provisions in trade agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide technical expertise during negotiations of multilateral and bilateral trade agreements (example: TPP), including drafting IP provisions and analyzing IP-related laws of partner states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectiveness can be judged by the strength and comprehensiveness of IP protections included in final agreements and USPTO involvement in negotiation/drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP Attaché deployment and engagement standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Post IP attachés in prioritized countries/regions and deploy them to play leadership roles in IPR working groups; conduct consultations, roundtables, meetings with stakeholders, and country-specific engagements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by number and placement of attachés, consultations organized, stakeholder meetings, and participation in action-plan implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: POA&M tracking and reduction goal (security remediation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track known security weaknesses requiring remediation using Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&M); the USPTO's goal is to decrease the number of open POA&Ms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 10 and Table 16 present counts (created/cancelled/completed/deleted) by FY/quarter; used to monitor cybersecurity remediation progress and risk posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital planning and IT investment control process
rubrics_metrics.description: In fulfilling 44 U.S.C. § 3504(h), the USPTO uses a capital planning and investment control process to prioritize investments and determine funding levels; projects managed through lifecycle with progress reviews at key milestones comparing status to planned benefit, cost, schedule, technical efficiency and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All major IT investments reported in OMB Circular A-11 Exhibit 53, Exhibit 300A, and 300B; use milestone reviews to compare actual vs planned performance and inform funding/prioritization decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: leverage IT investments (website, collaboration, availability, cloud)
rubrics_metrics.description: IT objectives include enhancing internal/external user experience via a new website and mobile portal, increasing collaboration and information-sharing (electronic interactions, web-conferencing), delivering '24/7/365' operational capability, evolving IT infrastructure via virtual and cloud capabilities, and delivering next-generation IT solutions and system integrations (PE2E, TMNG, FPNG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success measured by deployment of these capabilities, user adoption, functional parity with legacy systems, and improved customer transactions and internal workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAV deployment and usage metric
rubrics_metrics.description: DAV is the PE2E patent examiner case management tool; at end of FY 2016, 65% of patent examiners were using DAV three or more days per week; DAV achieved functional parity with legacy eDAN and eDAN scheduled to be phased out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage percentage and functional parity are criteria for replacing legacy systems; training and rollout plans expected as part of deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Correspondence and Examiner Search tools pilot/release criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Correspondence and Examiner Search tools targeted for initial release to patent examiners; pilot users evaluate available features prior to full rollout and examiner training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot feedback and readiness determine release timing and examiner training schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Management System (CMS) availability and disaster recovery requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PE2E's CMS was intended as a single, highly available content hub combining disparate patent document storage solutions; it must disperse large numbers of files in a highly available, distributed system that meets USPTO disaster recovery requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS experienced data storage/distribution obstacles and was rolled back; lessons learned drive evaluation of new solutions that meet availability and disaster recovery criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCommerce Modernization requirements (SSO, smart text XML)
rubrics_metrics.description: eCommerce modernization focuses on providing a cohesive login system via Single Sign On and receiving smart text (XML) versions of key patent application documents; prototypes were developed and evaluated by patent applicant beta testers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beta tester feedback informs product enhancements; meeting SSO and smart-text submission capabilities is a success criterion for the modernization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) harmonization and replacement criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: CPC maintains a Patent Classification Scheme harmonized between USPTO and EPO and automates collaboration for schema revisions; CPC should achieve functional parity with the legacy classification system and replace it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success measured by automation of collaboration, reduction in time for schema revisions, and attainment of functional parity enabling legacy retirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: TMNG migration and functional capability metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: TMNG accomplishments include migrating all content (5+ million images, 200+ million documents), deploying TMNG components (Synchronizer, Content Viewer), processing 6,300 office actions by beta testers, and demonstrating limited fail-over capability and external features (PDF certificates, ID Manual production).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics such as volume migrated, number of actions processed, synchronization capability, and fail-over demonstration are used to gauge readiness and capability of TMNG to replace legacy systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: FPNG deliverables (Financial Manager and Patent Maintenance Fees Storefront)
rubrics_metrics.description: Released Financial Manager and Patent Maintenance Fees Storefront to replace externally facing components of legacy fee-collection; features include storing/managing payment methods, user permissions, administrative notifications and reports, bulk fee upload and checkout, itemized receipts, and statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success measured by ability to replace legacy fee systems, adoption by customers, and secure single-user identity integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telework participation and impact metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure telework participation (number teleworking at least one day/week, percent of workforce teleworking, positions eligible to telework, TEAPP participants) and telework impacts (production rates during inclement weather, environmental metrics: miles avoided, gas savings, CO2 emissions reductions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate telework as a corporate strategy for efficiency, recruitment, retention, emergency continuity, and environmental benefits (e.g., FY2016: 10,567 teleworkers at least one day/week; production ~84%–85% of normal on inclement days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telework program management requirements and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Require teleworkers to review and electronically certify telework guidelines via computer-based training; distribute a telework management handbook; offer supervisory training 'Telework Tune Ups'; convene teleworker collaboration sessions (PaTH, TORCH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural controls and training interventions are intended to strengthen communication, collaboration, and effective remote workforce management and are prerequisites for program success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telework Enhancement Act Pilot Program (TEAPP) participation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: TEAPP allows employees to waive travel expenses for up to six mandatory trips to headquarters and permits hoteling (full-time teleworking) employees to elect to live >50 miles from USPTO by changing their official duty station; participation tracked (2,315 participants in FY2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program participation and policy compliance (waivers, duty station changes) are measurable outcomes supporting telework policy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation Challenge evaluation and selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency-wide competition with two rounds that welcomes individual/team submissions; round one yields top 20 ideas assessed by business unit and union leadership against several evaluation factors to select top five finalists; finalists develop business cases and present to senior leaders; final selection based on evaluation factors and feasibility for implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation factors (feasibility, impact, implementability) guide selection; voting, comments, and leadership assessment are used to measure idea merit and readiness for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: People Survey design and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO People Survey includes 63 diagnostic items across 14 dimensions, allows open-ended comments, measures response rate and engagement score (e.g., 61% response rate, 74% engagement score in FY2016), and identifies core strengths and areas for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey diagnostics feed action planning with executive management/union discussions; used to validate workforce engagement and inform targeted interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: After Work Education (AWE) program criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary program allowing eligible employees to take classes at an accredited college or university to develop work-related skills that improve current performance or enable advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses should be accredited and directly related to job performance or career development; outcomes measured by improved employee performance or readiness for other positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upward Mobility Program (UMP) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides career development opportunities for employees in positions with limited advancement; eligible employees apply for trainee positions, an Individual Training Plan (ITP) is developed, and upon successful ITP completion employees may be reassigned or non-competitively promoted to target positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful completion of the ITP is the criterion for reassignment/promotion; program measured by promotions and reassignments facilitated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Professionals Excellence (APEX) Program structure and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Nine-month voluntary curriculum for GS-5 through GS-12 technical and administrative staff combining live classroom, self-paced computer-based modules, mid-year review, and a capstone project, with networking opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program participation and capstone project completion are indicators of professional growth; designed to enhance career and personal development measurable via participant outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership Forum attendance and training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Bi-annual four-day Leadership Forum featuring keynote addresses and workshops aligned to pre-Forum survey priorities; managers required to attend 12 hours of training over four days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance and training-hour requirements establish minimum participation criteria; Forum success measured by exposure to best practices and application of insights in management.
